column3: When a test gives us bad news, we do something sneaky.
Students were tested for a made up health condition, with spit on a strip of paper.
Some were told: if the strip does not change color, that is bad news.
What they did not know: the strip was plain yellow paper. It never changed for anyone.
The bad news group took about thirty seconds longer to decide the test was done.
And over half of them retested. Some dipped the strip up to twelve times.
The good news group? Under one in five.
Good news, we accept instantly. Bad news has to prove itself.
Be honest. How many times would you dip?
